items.title: Class action claims women were raped and stalked at remote Fortescue mines
items.description: Andrew "Twiggy" Forrest's mining giant Fortescue has been slapped with a landmark class action alleging systemic sexual harassment, discrimination and toxic work sites.

items.title: Big battery boom means fewer transmission lines will be needed
items.description: Home batteries hit 600,000 as households play big role in energy transition, but building transmission projects remains "critical", according to the latest AEMO energy plan.

items.title: Former Liberal leader Matthew Guy denies assaulting MP Moira Deeming
items.description: Victorian MP Matthew Guy is considering legal advice to sue his party room colleague for defamation over the assault allegation, which is being investigated by police.

items.title: The highs and lows of Karl Stefanovic's 20 years with the Today show
items.description: Today show host Karl Stefanovic is reportedly leaving Channel Nine after a more than 20-year career at the network that was filled with highs and lows.

items.title: Teals Allegra Spender and Zali Steggall form new political party
items.description: The teal independents have confirmed they are forming a new political party, Community Strong Australia, but are yet to convince crossbench colleagues to join what they call a "responsible alternative" to the major parties.

items.title: Live: Coalition says it 'beggars belief' so-called ISIS-bride allowed back to Australia
items.description: Shadow Home Affairs Minister Jonathon Duniam says there are questions after a so-called ISIS bride, who was temporarily blocked from returning to Australia, received a permit to come back. Follow live.

items.title: Unemployment eases but trend rate hits four-year high
items.description: Australia's unemployment rate slipped to 4.4 per cent in May, down from 4.5 per cent in April, in seasonally adjusted terms.

items.title: The potentially deadly substance being delivered to Aussie doors at all hours
items.description: The importation of nitrous oxide has exploded in the last decade. Nangs are increasingly being used by some to chase a high and causing significant damage.

items.title: Live: Many casualties likely in Venezuela as buildings collapse in Caracas quakes
items.description: Buildings and houses collapse after a magnitude-7.2 earthquake strikes west of Caracas, leading scientists to estimate "high casualties and extensive damage" in the capital. Follow live.

items.title: Hanson's Socceroos own goal should have been a free kick for Taylor
items.description: Pauline Hanson has chosen one of Australia's most popular national sporting brands and visible expressions of cultural diversity in her pitch for a "monoculture".

items.title: Australians' tricks for dealing with heatwaves that Europeans yet to learn
items.description: Europe's record-breaking heatwave has highlighted its vulnerability to climate change. But countries could look to Australia's experience with scorching summers to learn valuable lessons.

items.title: Who is going to qualify for the World Cup knockout rounds?
items.description: The Socceroos will finish either second of third in their World Cup group. Second means qualification for the knockout rounds. Third is a bit more complicated.

items.title: Olympian arrested at reflecting pool is Trump 'scapegoat', lawyer says
items.description: A lawyer for the Olympian arrested at Washington's reflecting pool says his client is a scapegoat who was targeted to distract Americans from the Trump administration's failures.

items.title: 'Respected' 76yo pilot killed in plane crash built replica Spitfire himself
items.description: The friend of 76-year-old Malcolm Vivian, who died flying a light plane he built himself near Northam, describes his mate as a "very well-liked pilot" and "respected aircraft builder".

items.title: Taking the plunge in chilly winter water to tackle loneliness
items.description: Young people are turning to local community groups to get out of their comfort zones, make real connections and boost their wellbeing.

items.title: Ghost nets transformed into art to highlight pollution's 'devastating' impact
items.description: Thousands of tonnes of ocean waste lands on Australia's shores every year. These Queenslanders have found a creative use for some of it.

items.title: What pokies addict wishes she knew about gambling
items.description: Experts say the gambling industry is increasingly targeting women, and there are potential risks with a novelty bet.

items.title: As F1 heads to Austria the final result of Monaco goes to the courts
items.description: As F1 descends on the scenic Styrian Mountains for this weekend's Austrian Grand Prix, two teams are in the process of reversing the result in Monaco.

items.title: Live: ASX slips while gold futures drop below $US4,000 level
items.description: The unemployment rate has fallen to 4.4 per cent in May, down from 4.5 per cent in April. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: House prices in two Australian capitals tipped to fall substantially
items.description: House price falls of up to 7 and 8 per cent in Sydney and Melbourne have been forecast for the year ahead, according to Domain. But it is far from doom and gloom for existing owners, with resale profits hitting a record.

items.title: As Ebola spreads, Australia faces rise in 'biblical' disease risks
items.description: The bugs that cause Ebola, hantavirus and diphtheria are microscopic, but many of the barriers to controlling them are human-sized.

items.title: 86-year-old great-grandmother loves to 'thrash her ute' doing burnouts
items.description: Lorraine "Nan" Tuckett loves nothing more than letting the back end of her ute slide and smelling the rubber burn. She travels around Australia doing burnouts.

items.title: France and Vanuatu clash over remote Pacific island where 'god resides'
items.description: Tensions are rising between Vanuatu and France as they negotiate a sovereignty dispute over two volcanic islands, believed to be inhabited by a god.

items.title: Green back on happy hunting ground with chance to end golf-major drought
items.description: Australian Hannah Green is once again in sparkling form as she returns to the scene of her maiden major win in 2019 with hopes of ending ending her seven-year major drought.

items.title: Brisbane Broncos warn of scam offering fake mascot auditions
items.description: A scam is circulating online falsely offering fans a chance to audition to be the Brisbane Broncos' mascot in exchange for payment.
